content.title: MEAL PREP MISTAKES THAT QUIETLY KILL THE {{NUTRIENTS}}
facts: **Spinach** – boiling it in a big pot of water leaches out much of its folate and vitamin C; a quick steam or sauté keeps more intact.
**Tomatoes** – refrigerating them slows the natural process that boosts lycopene availability; room temperature storage works better.
**Bell Peppers** – long, slow cooking exposes vitamin C to heat for longer than a quick high-heat sear, so more of it breaks down.
**Lentils** – skipping a good rinse leaves surface starches behind that can make them harder to digest and more bloating-prone.
**Quinoa** – not rinsing it before cooking leaves the natural bitter coating on, which can also blunt mineral absorption.
**Salmon** – cooking it well past flaky causes a bigger drop in its delicate omega-3 fats than gentle baking or poaching does.
**Eggs** – cooking yolks until fully hard and browned reduces some of the antioxidants compared to a softer cook.
**Olive Oil** – heating it past its smoke point breaks down its beneficial compounds; save the good stuff for drizzling, not frying.
**Turmeric** – using it without any fat or black pepper in the dish means most of its curcumin just passes through unused.
**Kale** – letting cooked kale sit too long in cooking liquid drains a good amount of its vitamin K into the water instead of your plate.
**Follow along** – for more everyday fixes to how you cook, eat, and feel.
content.caption:
None of this means one overcooked salmon fillet or a fridge-cold tomato is undoing your healthy habits — it's more about small patterns over time. Everyone's kitchen, schedule, and body are different, so use these as gentle nudges rather than strict rules.

Follow @smarthealthfix for more on nutrition, common health issues, how your organs actually work, and the small daily habits that quietly add up.
